newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech brewer Plzensky Q1 97 loss CZK 17mln.
newsitem.headline: Czech brewer Plzensky Q1 97 loss CZK 17mln.

text.p: The largest Czech brewer, Plzensky Prazdroj a.s. said on Thursday it posted losses of 17 million crowns in the first quarter despite sharply rising output.
Preliminary results for three month period ending March 31, 1997 (in millions of crowns):

NOTE. The firm's shares are listed on the main market of the Prague Stock Exchange. Prazdroj, based in the western city of Plzen, had a 22 percent share of the beer market last year in the Czech Republic, which has the world's highest per capita beer consumption.
Prazdroj mainly brews lager-type beers such as Pilsner Urquell and Gambrinus. The company plans a net profit of 125 million crowns for the full year, after 75 million in 1996.
